sources_note:
SCOPE: national (Brazil-wide) polls of the 2026 presidential race whose results were published 27 Sep - 3 Oct 2026 (round 1, 1st-round question) or 18 - 24 Oct 2026 (round 2). State- and municipal-level polls registered under BR protocols (they ask the presidential question) are out of scope. Read 2026-10-26.

INDEX: pt.wikipedia "Pesquisas de opinião para a eleição presidencial no Brasil em 2026", revid 73293541 (2026-10-26T02:03:50Z), used only as an index; every number here was read from a primary or media source. The index has errors (see each poll's conflicts): Caiado/Renan columns swapped in several round-1 rows, valid-vote figures placed in total-vote columns (AtlasIntel and Futura, 3 Oct), a duplicate "DataFolha 1-3 Out, 2 002" row with no matching registration, the g1 sample 2.154 attached to Datafolha 20-22 Oct (it is the Quaest 17-20 Oct sample), and a 24 Oct Datafolha citation that points at a Jovem Pan article about BTG/Nexus.

REGISTRY: TSE open data (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br dataset pesquisas-eleitorais-2026), https://cdn.tse.jus.br/estatistica/sead/odsele/pesquisa_eleitoral/pesquisa_eleitoral_2026.zip (Last-Modified Mon, 26 Oct 2026 08:47:57 GMT, sha256 dd163dee1ae371dca6a4b09d17f230a7195c5f24c66dfdc052f8bcaeac0bd2d6; file pesquisa_eleitoral_2026_BRASIL.csv, generated 26/10/2026 05:47) and pesquisa_contratante_2026.zip (sha256 162bfe158cfa86e863264ea32c77deaeb3872a6ff872482c9d80b644a91e17df). Each poll's "registry" block copies its row (protocol, registered fieldwork and disclosure dates, planned sample, company, contractors, start of the methodology text). The registry holds what was REGISTERED (planned sample, planned dates); the published release can differ, and every difference is listed in "conflicts". The TSE PesqEle web consultation was not used.

VALUES: copied exactly as printed. The only normalizations: the "%" sign dropped and a decimal comma written as a dot ("40,4%" -> "40.4"); "<1" and the like kept. Nothing was computed, rounded or summed. valid_votes is null when the pollster did not publish valid votes; total_votes is null when only valid votes were found. Non-candidate categories (branco/nulo, não sabe, outros, nenhum) are under total_votes.other with their printed labels. Where a printed "Outros" is the sum of minor candidates also listed, the poll's notes say so; do not add both. Some valid-vote objects carry an "Outros" key as printed. Numbers read from chart images in pollster PDFs (rendered pages) are flagged in the source "what"; AtlasIntel 3 Oct and CNT/MDA 3 Oct chart labels were re-checked by a second reader. margin_of_error_pp and confidence_level_pct are as printed by the source (the registry's planned margin, when different, is in conflicts). method is coarse: in-person, phone (human CATI), phone-IVR (automated/URA), online.

CAVEATS for an exact check: (1) verita-r1-2026-09-30 is not one national sample but Veritá's reweighted consolidation of 27 state polls; it prints no national margin. (2) Tracking polls overlap: the two Gerp round-1 polls of 3 Oct share interviews; gerp-r2-2026-10-20 (3-day moving average 15-19 Oct, no registration printed) and gerp-r2-2026-10-21 print identical numbers; the two Veritá round-2 polls (18-22 and 19-23 Oct) overlap and report the same n. (3) Quaest's 3 Oct valid votes come from a likely-voter model (per g1), not from rescaling its totals; Datafolha 24 Oct also published propensity-weighted segments (other_published_scenarios). (4) PoderData round-2 sources print valid votes only.

EXCLUDED after checking: PoderData/Aya 23-24 Oct (BR-02828/2026) - published by Poder360 at 0h01 on 25 Oct, outside the window. Veritá 12-16 Oct (BR-01107/2026, registry disclosure 17 Oct) and Ipespe 13-15 Oct (BR-00223/2026, published 17 Oct) - before the window. Vetor Arrow 23-24 Oct (BR-06523, not in the TSE open data, due 26 Oct) and Phoenix 19-22 Oct (BR-06173, not in the TSE open data) - nothing published in the window was found. JOTA web poll (BR-05869/2026, registered disclosure 29 Sep) - no publication found. Instituto Seta (BR-07902, BR-08499), Badra, Ranking Brasil (MS), American Analytics (state polls) and the many state polls by Real Time Big Data, AtlasIntel, Veritá, Datafolha, Quaest, Instituto França and others - not national. The wiki's second "DataFolha 1-3 Out, 2 002" row - no registration, its headline matches the 3 Oct poll; treated as a duplicate.

GAPS: Veritá's final round-1 poll (26 Sep - 2 Oct, n 40.500, BR-04522/2026, published 3 Oct) - its only per-candidate source is an Instagram post that could not be read; later articles give only "about 47% / 45%" of valid votes; left out. Some polls rest on one source outside the preferred list (noted per poll): Palver 3 Oct (CartaCapital), Gerp 1-3 Oct (Jovem Pan), DataTrends (Blog Edmar Lyra), França 20 Oct (FanF1), Vetor Arrow (Agenda do Poder), Colectta and CNT/MDA 24 Oct (CartaCapital). UOL returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher, so UOL-cited polls were read from other outlets.
